title: Exploring the Performance Improvement of Tensor Processing Engines through Transformation in the Bit-weight Dimension of MACs
problem: Existing tensor processing engine (TPE) designs for GEMM focus on dataflow and operand reuse at the matrix level but neglect optimization opportunities within the multiply-accumulator (MAC) microarchitecture itself. There is no systematic framework for reasoning about and transforming the bit-level structure of MACs to improve TPE PPA.
motivation: As GEMM becomes the dominant compute primitive for AI workloads, TPEs are increasingly critical for both GPUs and domain-specific architectures, making MAC-level efficiency gains multiplicatively impactful.
method: The paper introduces a novel bit-weight dimension perspective on matrix multiplication and a finer-grained TPE notation based on matrix triple loops that exposes the internal MAC structure. Four optimization techniques are derived from transformations in this bit-weight space: they target timing, area, and power at the PE microarchitecture level. The design is implemented in RTL using SMIC-28nm and applied to four canonical TPE architectures (systolic array, 3D-Cube, multiplier-adder tree, 2D-Matrix) and a bit-slice architecture.
key_novelty: A new algebraic notation capturing the bit-weight dimension of MACs enables four distinct PE microarchitecture optimizations that are orthogonal to existing dataflow or operand-reuse strategies.
contributions: Novel bit-weight dimension perspective and finer-grained TPE notation based on matrix triple loops
Four optimization techniques targeting PE microarchitecture for improved timing, area, and power
RTL implementation in SMIC-28nm demonstrating 1.27-1.56x area efficiency and 1.04-1.56x energy efficiency across four classic TPE architectures
12.10x energy efficiency and 2.85x area efficiency improvement for a bit-slice architecture versus Laconic

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.04-1.56x energy efficiency vs. four classic TPEs; 12.10x vs. Laconic (bit-slice)
metrics.area: 1.27-1.56x area efficiency vs. four classic TPEs; 2.85x vs. Laconic (bit-slice)

primary_theme: MAC bit-weight dimension optimization for tensor processing engines
